BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook vs Seller counsel's Update draft and Disclosure Letter dated 22 September 2026

---

## 1. Threshold point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" preamble

Before the clause-by-clause review, one framing issue needs to be dealt with.

The Seller's preamble asserts that caps of 10–20%, baskets of ~1%, 12–18 month periods and buyer-knowledge qualifiers are "standard", that the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams", and that they are "marked FINAL and not intended to be re-opened".

**Our position:** We should not accept this characterisation.

- Our playbook is explicit that a 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and an 18-month period are *conditional fallbacks* available only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft, and that **no such authority has been given**. A seller-side statement that principals have agreed is not evidence of our principal's approval and does not change our mandate.
- The "market standard" ranges cited are the Seller's advocacy, not an agreed benchmark. They are also internally slanted — even on the Seller's own framing, their basket (AUD 250,000 ≈ 1.04%) and cap sit at or above the top of the quoted ranges, while fundamental warranties are collapsed into the general regime, which is not standard on any view.
- Our response should politely but clearly state that nothing is agreed or final until reflected in a signed SPA, that Wattlebridge's negotiating positions are as set out in our mark-up, and that we do not accept the Seller's description of prior principal-level agreement. If the Seller believes there was a principal conversation, ask them to identify it so we can verify with Amelia Frost directly.

**Action:** Confirm with Amelia Frost in writing that no fallback authority has been given on cap or claims period, so the deal team's record is clean.

---

## 2. Clause-by-clause: departures from playbook and recommended pushback

### 2.1 Clause 12.1 – General Warranty cap
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Cap | 20% / AUD 4,800,000 | 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (fallback 20% only with Frost written authority – not given) |

**Analysis:** The Seller has opened at exactly our *unauthorised* fallback. Conceding it now would spend our only fallback at the first exchange and leave nothing in reserve.
**Pushback:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal any willingness to move to 20% until and unless written authority is obtained.

### 2.2 Clause 12.2 – Thresholds (de minimis and basket)
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Basket type | Deductible (excess only) | Tipping (first-dollar once exceeded) |

**Analysis:** Three separate departures. The de minimis is 5× our position; the basket is 5× our position; and the basket is structured as a *deductible* rather than a *tipping* basket, which means the first AUD 250,000 of loss is permanently unrecoverable. The combination is significant for a SaaS business where individual warranty breaches (e.g. licence compliance, data/privacy, employee entitlements) tend to generate multiple mid-sized claims rather than a single large one.
**Pushback:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 basket; tipping (first-dollar) recovery. Resist the deductible structure as a matter of principle — it is a hidden additional cap.

### 2.3 Clause 12.3 / 13 – Time limits and the "all Claims" sweep
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months (18 months fallback only with Frost approval – not given) |
| Scope | "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override |

**Analysis:** Two issues:
1. **18 months** is again our unauthorised fallback. Counter at 24 months.
2. **The "all Claims" default is the more dangerous drafting.** It inverts the normal structure: instead of the general regime applying only to general Warranty Claims, every limitation (cap, basket, de minimis, time bar, knowledge exclusion) would by default attach to fundamental warranties, tax, IP, specific indemnities (including Ironquay), payment obligations and covenants, unless we spot and carve out each one. This is precisely the "hidden general-regime override" the playbook prohibits.
**Pushback:** Reverse the default. The general limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims as defined. Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenant breaches and payment obligations each have their own expressly stated regime (or none).

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Treatment | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% of price cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar |

**Analysis:** This is a material departure and should be treated as non-negotiable. Capacity and title go to whether we acquire the asset at all. If the Seller does not own the shares, or lacks authority to sell, a 20% cap and an 18-month tail leave us with a AUD 19.2m uncompensated hole. "Administrative simplicity" is not a commercial justification. This is also not market practice on any reasonable view, which further undermines the preamble's "standard terms" claim.
**Pushback:** Separate Fundamental Warranties schedule; cap at 100% of price (AUD 24,000,000); minimum 6-year claims period; expressly outside the de minimis, basket and any knowledge qualifier.

### 2.5 Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature"
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct | No carve-out stated; limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this |

**Analysis:** The draft contains **no fraud carve-out at all**, and the "all Claims of any nature" language would purport to extend caps, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to fraudulent conduct. Beyond being contrary to playbook, a clause purporting to exclude liability for the Seller's own fraud is of doubtful enforceability under NSW law and is reputationally untenable to accept. The exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses also need checking against the Australian Consumer Law (misleading or deceptive conduct) – a bare non-reliance clause will not exclude statutory liability, and the drafting should not pretend otherwise.
**Pushback:** Insert an express, non-waivable carve-out: none of the limitations in clause 12, the exclusive-remedy clause or the non-reliance clause applies to fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct by the Seller, the Company or their officers/advisers. Narrow 9.3/12.8/20.5 to the categories they are meant to govern.

### 2.6 Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – General disclosure
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Method | Whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012) + Accounts + statutory registers + "publicly searchable corporate records" deemed disclosed | Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure |

**Analysis:** Paragraphs [1.1] and [1.2] are exactly the general disclosure the playbook rejects. Whole-data-room disclosure means every warranty is qualified by anything buried anywhere in the data room, whether or not it was fairly flagged. "Publicly searchable corporate records" is open-ended and would extend to matters we had no reason to search. Note also para [1.4] – a blanket denial that anything disclosed amounts to an admission that any consent, payment or remediation is required. That is acceptable as a non-admission, but it cannot be allowed to undercut the specific undertakings we will require (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses).
**Pushback:** Delete [1.1]–[1.2] general disclosure. Replace with a "fair disclosure" standard: a matter is disclosed only if disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Specific data room documents may be referenced against specific warranties.

### 2.7 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge exclusion
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | No claim for any matter of which Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, including anything *discoverable* from data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities |

**Analysis:** This is a blanket constructive-knowledge bar. "Discoverable from the data room or public records" is not actual knowledge – it is a deemed-knowledge standard that would effectively convert the data room into a universal defence and import the adviser team's awareness. Combined with 2.6, it would hollow out the warranty package. It also cuts across our title and specific-indemnity positions.
**Pushback:** Delete 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it should be a *seller* knowledge qualifier (named individuals, after due and careful enquiry) attached to specific warranties – not a buyer knowledge exclusion. Expressly state that no knowledge of the Buyer or its advisers limits claims for title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### 2.8 Clauses 3 / 6.3 – Bluefen consent (≈AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, ~30%)
| | Seller | Playbook / Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" | Effective consent AND evidence clause 11.3 conditions satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient |
| Status | — | DL para 2: no final written consent and no evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied |

**Analysis:** Bluefen is ~30% of revenue – this is a value-critical condition. The Seller's draft is deficient in two ways: (i) "reasonable endeavours" is too low a standard for the single most material customer consent; and (ii) "satisfied on delivery" means a consent letter that is itself conditional on unsatisfied 11.3 conditions would still tick the box. The Disclosure Letter confirms neither the consent nor the condition evidence exists yet.
**Pushback:** Condition precedent: delivery of Bluefen's written consent under clause 11.2 *in form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer*, together with evidence that each clause 11.3 condition has been satisfied (or waived by Bluefen in writing), before Completion. Upgrade the obligation to "all reasonable endeavours" / "best endeavours" with specific steps. Consider a Bluefen-specific indemnity or price adjustment mechanism if consent is delayed or conditional.

### 2.9 Clauses 2 / 7 – Riverlark Bank facility (≈AUD 3.2m)
| | Seller | Playbook / Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanism | Release "to be provided following Completion" | Current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval |
| Status | — | DL para 3: not repaid; no final discharge included |

**Analysis:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, a AUD 3.2m facility with security left in place post-Completion is a direct value leak and a lender-control risk. DD-003 also records a change-of-control trigger (8.1), so Completion without a release may itself be an event of default. A post-completion release with no undertaking is unacceptable.
**Pushback:** Completion deliverables to include: (i) Riverlark payout letter stating the exact amount as at Completion; (ii) funds flow directing that amount from the purchase price to Riverlark; (iii) executed releases/discharges of all security (including PPSR discharges and release of any guarantees) delivered at Completion or held in escrow against receipt of funds. Any residual post-completion mechanics require an irrevocable lender undertaking and Amelia Frost's written approval.

### 2.10 Funds flow – DD-005 employee bonuses (AUD 420,000 + on-costs)
| | Seller | Playbook / Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Treatment | "A matter for the Seller"; not itemised in funds flow | Specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them |
| Status | — | DL para 5: AUD 420,000 conditional on Completion and continued employment; not in funds flow; on-costs not addressed |

**Analysis:** These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the *Company* (which we will own), not of the Seller. "A matter for the Seller" is not a mechanism – once the bonuses vest on Completion, the Company pays, and the Buyer bears the cost unless the price mechanics capture it. Payroll tax and superannuation on AUD 420,000 could add a material further amount. Silence in the funds flow is exactly the outcome the playbook warns against.
**Pushback:** Either (a) treat the gross bonus plus all employer on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, leave accrual impact) as Debt/Transaction Costs deducted from the price, or (b) require the Seller to fund them directly to the Company at Completion via a specific line item in the funds flow. Obtain the Seller's calculation of on-costs.

### 2.11 Clause 11.1 – Ironquay IP indemnity
| | Seller | Playbook / Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | Limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" | Broaden the indemnity; preserve the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way |
| Status | — | DL para 4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open (internal record, not bank-verified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room |

**Analysis:** The risk is not just the AUD 180,000 – it is that title to the SOW3 Project Materials (which may be embedded in the product) has not passed and will not pass until payment clears. An indemnity limited to the payment amount does not cover loss of IP ownership, injunction risk, re-engineering costs or third-party claims. Note also that under the Seller's "all Claims" default (2.3), this indemnity would be capped and time-barred. We should not assume the AUD 180,000 is unpaid, nor that it is paid.
**Pushback:** (i) Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay (preserving the clause 7.3 cure). (ii) Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of IP in the Project Materials to vest in the Company, including third-party claims, injunctive relief and remediation. (iii) Expressly outside the general cap, basket and time limits.

### 2.12 Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 – Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
| | Seller | Playbook / Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Characterisation | "Preliminary operational matter"; "not expected to be material" | Preserve logs; investigate; require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way |
| Status | — | DL para 6: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) sent to unintended external address; access/scope/notification not yet established |

**Analysis:** Our playbook is deliberately neutral – we should neither accept the Seller's "not material" conclusion nor assert that a notifiable breach has occurred. The point is that the investigation is incomplete, so no conclusion is yet available. The data types involved (business contact data) may or may not meet the Notifiable Data Breaches threshold depending on access and harm – that assessment is outstanding.
**Pushback:** (i) Pre-Completion covenant: Seller to procure that the Company preserves all relevant logs and records, completes the investigation (including access logs for the link), and provides written updates and the final report before Completion. (ii) Warranty that the Disclosure Letter description is accurate and complete as at Completion. (iii) Specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident, outside the general caps/basket, with no admission either way as to breach or notification. (iv) Reserve position on materiality pending the report.

### 2.13 Supplier renewals – Sandbar (AUD 330,000)
| | Seller | Playbook / Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Treatment | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction |
| Status | — | DL para 8: three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; DD-008 and DD-011 to be read together; unclear whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued, or ordinary course |

**Analysis:** The Seller's characterisation may well be right, but it is asserted without the facts needed to confirm it. We should not reflexively treat these as Debt either.
**Pushback:** Request: renewal dates, termination rights, whether any of the AUD 330,000 is accrued or prepaid at Completion, and whether the three are a single commitment split into tranches. Treat as a working-capital / completion-accounts point unless the facts show a non-ordinary-course commitment, in which case revisit classification.

### 2.14 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Treatment | Settled; subject to general cap/basket/18-month regime | OPEN; separate category; no unlimited liability and no resolution assumed |

**Analysis:** The Seller is attempting to close these by folding them into the general regime (reinforced by the 2.3 "all Claims" sweep). Our playbook says these remain open. We should not accept either the 18-month/20% treatment or, equally, assume an unlimited tax indemnity – we simply have not yet agreed.
**Pushback:** State that Tax and IP warranty/indemnity terms remain open and will be addressed separately with their own cap and claims period (Tax typically tracking the statutory assessment period plus a margin). Reject their inclusion in clause 13's default sweep.

### 2.15 Title evidence – DD-012 share register
| | Seller | Playbook / Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence | Share register at DD-012 | Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof |
| Status | — | DL para 10: Seller acknowledges DD-012 is the source relied on and Buyer has not completed its own verification |

**Analysis:** A company-maintained share register is prima facie but not independent evidence. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter concedes we have not verified title. This dovetails with 2.4 – if title is weak, a capped and time-limited title warranty is doubly inadequate.
**Pushback:** Pre-Completion/Completion deliverables: current ASIC company extract; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller showing no security over the shares (or releases for any found – cross-check Riverlark); copies of the share certificate(s); Seller board and (if required) shareholder resolutions approving the sale; constitution to confirm no pre-emption or transfer restrictions; and officer's certificates. Retain our full fundamental warranty regime regardless.

---

## 3. Additional Disclosure Letter points

- **Office lease (DL para 7, DD-007):** Disclosed as a notification obligation, not a consent requirement. Accept the characterisation provisionally but require the notification to be given (or a covenant to give it) and a warranty that no landlord consent is required for a share sale.
- **Mossvale (DL para 9, DD-009):** Assignment restriction not triggered by share sale on the Seller's reading. Confirm by reviewing DD-009 for any change-of-control language; obtain a warranty that no Mossvale consent is required.
- **Paragraph [1.4] (non-admission) and [11] (reservation):** Acceptable as drafting, but ensure they do not operate to qualify the specific pre-Completion deliverables we require on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and the bonuses.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Reject the "FINAL / principal-agreed" framing.** Record in our response that nothing is agreed, that no Wattlebridge fallback authority exists on cap or claims period, and that the preamble's "market standard" statements are not accepted.

**Priority 1 – structural / non-negotiable**
1. Fundamental/Title warranties: separate regime, 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
2. Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct: express, non-waivable carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
3. Reverse the clause 13 "all Claims" default so general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims; Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenants and payment obligations each separately addressed.
4. Delete clause 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion and the general data-room / public-record disclosure in Schedule 7 / DL [1.1]–[1.2]; substitute specific fair disclosure.

**Priority 2 – economic terms (hold at playbook opening positions)**
5. Cap: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
6. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping (first-dollar) basket.
7. General claims period: 24 months.

**Priority 3 – completion mechanics and specific risks**
8. Bluefen: CP requiring effective written consent plus evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; upgrade endeavours standard.
9. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, security releases at Completion; no post-completion release without irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
10. DD-005 bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded; obtain on-cost calculation.
11. Ironquay: evidence of cleared SOW3 payment and confirmatory assignment; broaden indemnity to cover IP vesting failure; outside general caps.
12. DD-006 incident: log preservation, completed investigation and updates before Completion; specific indemnity; reserve on materiality with no assumption of breach or non-breach.
13. Sandbar: request facts; assess under working capital; no automatic Debt treatment.
14. Title: independent evidence (ASIC extract, PPSR, certificates, authorisations, constitution review).
15. Tax / IP: expressly OPEN; to be settled in separate regimes.

**Internal action:** Obtain written confirmation from Amelia Frost that no fallback authority has been granted, so the record is clear before the mark-up goes to the Seller.

The Seller's preamble asserts that caps of 10–20%, baskets of ~1%, 12–18 month periods and buyer-knowledge qualifiers are "standard", that the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams", and that they are "marked FINAL and not intended to be re-opened".

**Our position:** We should not accept this characterisation.

- Our playbook is explicit that a 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and an 18-month period are *conditional fallbacks* available only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft, and that **no such authority has been given**. A seller-side statement that principals have agreed is not evidence of our principal's approval and does not change our mandate.
- The "market standard" ranges cited are the Seller's advocacy, not an agreed benchmark. They are also internally slanted — even on the Seller's own framing, their basket (AUD 250,000 ≈ 1.04%) and cap sit at or above the top of the quoted ranges, while fundamental warranties are collapsed into the general regime, which is not standard on any view.
- Our response should politely but clearly state that nothing is agreed or final until reflected in a signed SPA, that Wattlebridge's negotiating positions are as set out in our mark-up, and that we do not accept the Seller's description of prior principal-level agreement. If the Seller believes there was a principal conversation, ask them to identify it so we can verify with Amelia Frost directly.

**Action:** Confirm with Amelia Frost in writing that no fallback authority has been given on cap or claims period, so the deal team's record is clean.

## 2. Clause-by-clause: departures from playbook and recommended pushback

### 2.1 Clause 12.1 – General Warranty cap
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Cap | 20% / AUD 4,800,000 | 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (fallback 20% only with Frost written authority – not given) |

**Analysis:** The Seller has opened at exactly our *unauthorised* fallback. Conceding it now would spend our only fallback at the first exchange and leave nothing in reserve.
**Pushback:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal any willingness to move to 20% until and unless written authority is obtained.

### 2.2 Clause 12.2 – Thresholds (de minimis and basket)
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Basket type | Deductible (excess only) | Tipping (first-dollar once exceeded) |

**Analysis:** Three separate departures. The de minimis is 5× our position; the basket is 5× our position; and the basket is structured as a *deductible* rather than a *tipping* basket, which means the first AUD 250,000 of loss is permanently unrecoverable. The combination is significant for a SaaS business where individual warranty breaches (e.g. licence compliance, data/privacy, employee entitlements) tend to generate multiple mid-sized claims rather than a single large one.
**Pushback:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 basket; tipping (first-dollar) recovery. Resist the deductible structure as a matter of principle — it is a hidden additional cap.

### 2.3 Clause 12.3 / 13 – Time limits and the "all Claims" sweep
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months (18 months fallback only with Frost approval – not given) |
| Scope | "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override |

**Analysis:** Two issues:
1. **18 months** is again our unauthorised fallback. Counter at 24 months.
2. **The "all Claims" default is the more dangerous drafting.** It inverts the normal structure: instead of the general regime applying only to general Warranty Claims, every limitation (cap, basket, de minimis, time bar, knowledge exclusion) would by default attach to fundamental warranties, tax, IP, specific indemnities (including Ironquay), payment obligations and covenants, unless we spot and carve out each one. This is precisely the "hidden general-regime override" the playbook prohibits.
**Pushback:** Reverse the default. The general limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims as defined. Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenant breaches and payment obligations each have their own expressly stated regime (or none).

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Treatment | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% of price cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar |

**Analysis:** This is a material departure and should be treated as non-negotiable. Capacity and title go to whether we acquire the asset at all. If the Seller does not own the shares, or lacks authority to sell, a 20% cap and an 18-month tail leave us with a AUD 19.2m uncompensated hole. "Administrative simplicity" is not a commercial justification. This is also not market practice on any reasonable view, which further undermines the preamble's "standard terms" claim.
**Pushback:** Separate Fundamental Warranties schedule; cap at 100% of price (AUD 24,000,000); minimum 6-year claims period; expressly outside the de minimis, basket and any knowledge qualifier.

### 2.5 Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature"
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct | No carve-out stated; limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this |

**Analysis:** The draft contains **no fraud carve-out at all**, and the "all Claims of any nature" language would purport to extend caps, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to fraudulent conduct. Beyond being contrary to playbook, a clause purporting to exclude liability for the Seller's own fraud is of doubtful enforceability under NSW law and is reputationally untenable to accept. The exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses also need checking against the Australian Consumer Law (misleading or deceptive conduct) – a bare non-reliance clause will not exclude statutory liability, and the drafting should not pretend otherwise.
**Pushback:** Insert an express, non-waivable carve-out: none of the limitations in clause 12, the exclusive-remedy clause or the non-reliance clause applies to fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct by the Seller, the Company or their officers/advisers. Narrow 9.3/12.8/20.5 to the categories they are meant to govern.

### 2.6 Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – General disclosure
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Method | Whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012) + Accounts + statutory registers + "publicly searchable corporate records" deemed disclosed | Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure |

**Analysis:** Paragraphs [1.1] and [1.2] are exactly the general disclosure the playbook rejects. Whole-data-room disclosure means every warranty is qualified by anything buried anywhere in the data room, whether or not it was fairly flagged. "Publicly searchable corporate records" is open-ended and would extend to matters we had no reason to search. Note also para [1.4] – a blanket denial that anything disclosed amounts to an admission that any consent, payment or remediation is required. That is acceptable as a non-admission, but it cannot be allowed to undercut the specific undertakings we will require (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses).
**Pushback:** Delete [1.1]–[1.2] general disclosure. Replace with a "fair disclosure" standard: a matter is disclosed only if disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Specific data room documents may be referenced against specific warranties.

### 2.7 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge exclusion
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | No claim for any matter of which Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, including anything *discoverable* from data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities |

**Analysis:** This is a blanket constructive-knowledge bar. "Discoverable from the data room or public records" is not actual knowledge – it is a deemed-knowledge standard that would effectively convert the data room into a universal defence and import the adviser team's awareness. Combined with 2.6, it would hollow out the warranty package. It also cuts across our title and specific-indemnity positions.
**Pushback:** Delete 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it should be a *seller* knowledge qualifier (named individuals, after due and careful enquiry) attached to specific warranties – not a buyer knowledge exclusion. Expressly state that no knowledge of the Buyer or its advisers limits claims for title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### 2.8 Clauses 3 / 6.3 – Bluefen consent (≈AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, ~30%)
| | Seller | Playbook / Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" | Effective consent AND evidence clause 11.3 conditions satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient |
| Status | — | DL para 2: no final written consent and no evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied |

**Analysis:** Bluefen is ~30% of revenue – this is a value-critical condition. The Seller's draft is deficient in two ways: (i) "reasonable endeavours" is too low a standard for the single most material customer consent; and (ii) "satisfied on delivery" means a consent letter that is itself conditional on unsatisfied 11.3 conditions would still tick the box. The Disclosure Letter confirms neither the consent nor the condition evidence exists yet.
**Pushback:** Condition precedent: delivery of Bluefen's written consent under clause 11.2 *in form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer*, together with evidence that each clause 11.3 condition has been satisfied (or waived by Bluefen in writing), before Completion. Upgrade the obligation to "all reasonable endeavours" / "best endeavours" with specific steps. Consider a Bluefen-specific indemnity or price adjustment mechanism if consent is delayed or conditional.

### 2.9 Clauses 2 / 7 – Riverlark Bank facility (≈AUD 3.2m)
| | Seller | Playbook / Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanism | Release "to be provided following Completion" | Current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval |
| Status | — | DL para 3: not repaid; no final discharge included |

**Analysis:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, a AUD 3.2m facility with security left in place post-Completion is a direct value leak and a lender-control risk. DD-003 also records a change-of-control trigger (8.1), so Completion without a release may itself be an event of default. A post-completion release with no undertaking is unacceptable.
**Pushback:** Completion deliverables to include: (i) Riverlark payout letter stating the exact amount as at Completion; (ii) funds flow directing that amount from the purchase price to Riverlark; (iii) executed releases/discharges of all security (including PPSR discharges and release of any guarantees) delivered at Completion or held in escrow against receipt of funds. Any residual post-completion mechanics require an irrevocable lender undertaking and Amelia Frost's written approval.

### 2.10 Funds flow – DD-005 employee bonuses (AUD 420,000 + on-costs)
| | Seller | Playbook / Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Treatment | "A matter for the Seller"; not itemised in funds flow | Specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them |
| Status | — | DL para 5: AUD 420,000 conditional on Completion and continued employment; not in funds flow; on-costs not addressed |

**Analysis:** These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the *Company* (which we will own), not of the Seller. "A matter for the Seller" is not a mechanism – once the bonuses vest on Completion, the Company pays, and the Buyer bears the cost unless the price mechanics capture it. Payroll tax and superannuation on AUD 420,000 could add a material further amount. Silence in the funds flow is exactly the outcome the playbook warns against.
**Pushback:** Either (a) treat the gross bonus plus all employer on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, leave accrual impact) as Debt/Transaction Costs deducted from the price, or (b) require the Seller to fund them directly to the Company at Completion via a specific line item in the funds flow. Obtain the Seller's calculation of on-costs.

### 2.11 Clause 11.1 – Ironquay IP indemnity
| | Seller | Playbook / Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | Limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" | Broaden the indemnity; preserve the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way |
| Status | — | DL para 4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open (internal record, not bank-verified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room |

**Analysis:** The risk is not just the AUD 180,000 – it is that title to the SOW3 Project Materials (which may be embedded in the product) has not passed and will not pass until payment clears. An indemnity limited to the payment amount does not cover loss of IP ownership, injunction risk, re-engineering costs or third-party claims. Note also that under the Seller's "all Claims" default (2.3), this indemnity would be capped and time-barred. We should not assume the AUD 180,000 is unpaid, nor that it is paid.
**Pushback:** (i) Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay (preserving the clause 7.3 cure). (ii) Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of IP in the Project Materials to vest in the Company, including third-party claims, injunctive relief and remediation. (iii) Expressly outside the general cap, basket and time limits.

### 2.12 Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 – Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
| | Seller | Playbook / Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Characterisation | "Preliminary operational matter"; "not expected to be material" | Preserve logs; investigate; require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way |
| Status | — | DL para 6: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) sent to unintended external address; access/scope/notification not yet established |

**Analysis:** Our playbook is deliberately neutral – we should neither accept the Seller's "not material" conclusion nor assert that a notifiable breach has occurred. The point is that the investigation is incomplete, so no conclusion is yet available. The data types involved (business contact data) may or may not meet the Notifiable Data Breaches threshold depending on access and harm – that assessment is outstanding.
**Pushback:** (i) Pre-Completion covenant: Seller to procure that the Company preserves all relevant logs and records, completes the investigation (including access logs for the link), and provides written updates and the final report before Completion. (ii) Warranty that the Disclosure Letter description is accurate and complete as at Completion. (iii) Specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident, outside the general caps/basket, with no admission either way as to breach or notification. (iv) Reserve position on materiality pending the report.

### 2.13 Supplier renewals – Sandbar (AUD 330,000)
| | Seller | Playbook / Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Treatment | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction |
| Status | — | DL para 8: three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; DD-008 and DD-011 to be read together; unclear whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued, or ordinary course |

**Analysis:** The Seller's characterisation may well be right, but it is asserted without the facts needed to confirm it. We should not reflexively treat these as Debt either.
**Pushback:** Request: renewal dates, termination rights, whether any of the AUD 330,000 is accrued or prepaid at Completion, and whether the three are a single commitment split into tranches. Treat as a working-capital / completion-accounts point unless the facts show a non-ordinary-course commitment, in which case revisit classification.

### 2.14 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Treatment | Settled; subject to general cap/basket/18-month regime | OPEN; separate category; no unlimited liability and no resolution assumed |

**Analysis:** The Seller is attempting to close these by folding them into the general regime (reinforced by the 2.3 "all Claims" sweep). Our playbook says these remain open. We should not accept either the 18-month/20% treatment or, equally, assume an unlimited tax indemnity – we simply have not yet agreed.
**Pushback:** State that Tax and IP warranty/indemnity terms remain open and will be addressed separately with their own cap and claims period (Tax typically tracking the statutory assessment period plus a margin). Reject their inclusion in clause 13's default sweep.

### 2.15 Title evidence – DD-012 share register
| | Seller | Playbook / Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence | Share register at DD-012 | Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof |
| Status | — | DL para 10: Seller acknowledges DD-012 is the source relied on and Buyer has not completed its own verification |

**Analysis:** A company-maintained share register is prima facie but not independent evidence. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter concedes we have not verified title. This dovetails with 2.4 – if title is weak, a capped and time-limited title warranty is doubly inadequate.
**Pushback:** Pre-Completion/Completion deliverables: current ASIC company extract; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller showing no security over the shares (or releases for any found – cross-check Riverlark); copies of the share certificate(s); Seller board and (if required) shareholder resolutions approving the sale; constitution to confirm no pre-emption or transfer restrictions; and officer's certificates. Retain our full fundamental warranty regime regardless.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Reject the "FINAL / principal-agreed" framing.** Record in our response that nothing is agreed, that no Wattlebridge fallback authority exists on cap or claims period, and that the preamble's "market standard" statements are not accepted.

**Priority 1 – structural / non-negotiable**
1. Fundamental/Title warranties: separate regime, 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
2. Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct: express, non-waivable carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
3. Reverse the clause 13 "all Claims" default so general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims; Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenants and payment obligations each separately addressed.
4. Delete clause 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion and the general data-room / public-record disclosure in Schedule 7 / DL [1.1]–[1.2]; substitute specific fair disclosure.

**Priority 2 – economic terms (hold at playbook opening positions)**
5. Cap: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
6. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping (first-dollar) basket.
7. General claims period: 24 months.

**Priority 3 – completion mechanics and specific risks**
8. Bluefen: CP requiring effective written consent plus evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; upgrade endeavours standard.
9. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, security releases at Completion; no post-completion release without irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
10. DD-005 bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded; obtain on-cost calculation.
11. Ironquay: evidence of cleared SOW3 payment and confirmatory assignment; broaden indemnity to cover IP vesting failure; outside general caps.
12. DD-006 incident: log preservation, completed investigation and updates before Completion; specific indemnity; reserve on materiality with no assumption of breach or non-breach.
13. Sandbar: request facts; assess under working capital; no automatic Debt treatment.
14. Title: independent evidence (ASIC extract, PPSR, certificates, authorisations, constitution review).
15. Tax / IP: expressly OPEN; to be settled in separate regimes.

**Internal action:** Obtain written confirmation from Amelia Frost that no fallback authority has been granted, so the record is clear before the mark-up goes to the Seller.
